narrative: Comprehensive inventory optimization analysis for material PL1__MCD7ED62 reveals an intermittent demand pattern with 57.1% working days showing positive demand. The demand exhibits gamma-like distribution characteristics with coefficient of variation 1.05, indicating moderate volatility. Mean daily demand is 140.81 units with standard deviation 147.97. Lead time analysis shows unstable behavior (CV=1.29) with mean 0.60 days and effective lead time (including buffer) of 1.39 days. The optimized policy recommends increasing safety stock from 180 to 262 units (+45.6%) while significantly increasing order quantity from 257 to 3260 units to achieve economies of scale. This consolidation reduces annual ordering frequency from 142.5 to 11.2 orders per year, generating total cost savings of $6015.53 (83.2%). The reorder point is set at 458 units to maintain 95% service level, with a recommended review period of 24 days. Current SAP safety lead time of 4.0 days appears conservative; statistical analysis suggests reducing to 1.29 days based on observed variability.
research_insights: Academic research on intermittent demand patterns (Syntetos & Boylan, 2005) emphasizes the importance of robust forecasting methods that account for both demand occurrence and magnitude variability. The gamma-like distribution observed aligns with findings in Willemain et al. (2004) on industrial spare parts demand. Lead time variability with CV>1.0 indicates supply chain instability requiring enhanced buffer strategies (Chopra & Sodhi, 2004). The high ordering cost relative to holding cost justifies larger, less frequent orders consistent with EOQ theory (Harris, 1913; Wilson, 1934). Research by Silver et al. (2016) demonstrates that periodic review systems with (s,S) policies perform well for intermittent demand when properly calibrated. The 70-30 decomposition of lead time variance between transport and supplier factors follows supply chain risk frameworks by Christopher & Peck (2004). Modern inventory optimization increasingly leverages machine learning for demand sensing (Boone et al., 2019), though traditional statistical methods remain robust for service level targeting. The significant cost savings potential (>80%) from policy optimization demonstrates the value of data-driven inventory management, as quantified in studies by Katehakis & Smit (2012) on optimal replenishment policies under uncertainty.
